result:
No actions this turn. One step remains before I write the design: choosing how to build it.

---

Thanks. That's everything I need about *what* you want. I'll write it up next. One thing is still open, and it shapes the whole document: *how* it gets built. It's a quick pick.

1. **Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** The batch records go into the Flask app that already runs on the Pi. They live in their own part of the code. A USB barcode scanner acts like a keyboard, so a scan fills a field on a web page without any typing. You still have one program to run and one place to back up.
   - *Trade-off:* the taproom tabs and the batch records share one program. A bad update to one can take down the other until it's fixed.
2. **A separate small app on the same Pi.** It uses the same tools but runs as its own program with its own database.
   - *Trade-off:* a tab bug can't touch your traceability records. But you have two programs to update and two databases to back up.
3. **Buy brewery software.** Some hosted services already do batch and lot tracking.
   - *Trade-off:* you pay a monthly fee and need the internet to log a sack. I'd also have to check whether they work with your label printer.

I recommend option 1. It's the least to run and look after on one Pi, and keeping the batch code separate limits the coupling.

This is a project-sized piece of work, so I'll write a full design document. Before I hand it to you, a reviewer will read it as the builder would. I may come back once with a few questions from that review.

Which way do you want to go: option 1, or one of the others?
